newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shrs drift to lower close despite strong bonds.
newsitem.headline: NZ shrs drift to lower close despite strong bonds.

text.p: * NZ shares close weaker despite strong bond market
* Election uncertainties seen weighing on market
New Zealand shares drifted to a lower close on Thursday in spite of lower bond yields, which brokers noted would normally prompt investment in equities.
The NZSE-40 Capital index shed 9.84 points to 2234.26.

"There's a bit of selling coming out," said Tim Koller and Hendry Hay McIntosh. "I don't know whether it's people starting to get a little bit more nervous before the election; it could well be." A general election will be held on October 12.
Brokers said equities had failed to respond to a stronger bond market, which rallied for the second day in succession.
Most of the leaders posted losses, but Carter Holt Harvey was the main impediment for the top-40 index on the day, falling seven cents to $3.29.
Brokers said there had been a negative newspaper report on Carter Holt in the United States and also pointed to a weaker S&P paper index as reasons for the forester's seven cent demise.
"But on the other hand we've seen good demand in Fletcher forest and Fletcher Paper," Koller said. Fletcher Forest was up two cents at $2.13, as was Fletcher Paper at $2.87.
However, Ceramco Corp slid 11 cents to a new low of $1.15, which brokers attributed to the company's announcement last week that it expects a net loss for the half year to September.
Brokers said offshore interest in New Zealand equities was muted on the day, and Koller predicted continued weakness in the share market as the election neared.
"Bonds can't go much further, so if you get that turning around as well, that will exacerbate things.
"It's feasible that we could slip back five percent between now and the election," he said.
